section_1.title: The Core Intuition: The 'It' Problem
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental problem of context in language. Explain how humans focus on specific words to understand meaning. Use a simple sentence to show how the word 'it' changes meaning based on the surrounding context.
section_1.example: Consider the sentences: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired' vs 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too wide'. In the first, 'it' is the animal; in the second, 'it' is the street. Attention is the mechanism that allows a computer to 'look' at the right words to figure this out.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors
section_2.content: Introduce vectors as arrows in space representing meaning. Explain the 'Dot Product' as a graphical tool: when two arrows point in the same direction, their product is high (they are similar). This is the mathematical 'glue' of attention.
section_2.example: Visualize two arrows: 'Apple' and 'Fruit' pointing almost in the same direction (high score), while 'Apple' and 'Hammer' point in opposite directions (low score).

section_3.title: The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
section_3.content: Define the three roles each word plays using a 'Library Search' analogy. 1. Query (Q): What I am looking for. 2. Key (K): The label on the shelf. 3. Value (V): The actual information inside the book.
section_3.example: Imagine a Golden Retriever (the Query) looking for 'Food'. He checks various items (Keys): a 'Ball', a 'Leash', and a 'Bowl of Kibble'. The 'Bowl of Kibble' Key matches his Query best, so he focuses his attention on the contents (Value) of that bowl.

section_4.title: The Step-by-Step Calculation
section_4.content: Break down the Attention formula: Score = (Q × K). Then, apply 'Softmax' to turn scores into percentages (weights) that add up to 100%. Finally, multiply these percentages by V to get the focused output. Use a heatmap visualization.
section_4.example: In the sentence 'The cat sat', when processing 'cat', the Q(cat) hits K(the) with 10% weight and K(sat) with 20% weight, but K(cat) itself with 70%. The resulting vector is a weighted mix of all three, heavily biased toward 'cat's' own identity and 'sat's' action.

section_5.title: Multi-Head Attention: Multiple Perspectives
section_5.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough. LLMs use 'Multi-Head Attention' to look at different relationships simultaneously (e.g., grammar, rhyme, logic). Visualize this as several different colored spotlights shining on the same text.
section_5.example: Head 1 (Red light) focuses on 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb). Head 2 (Blue light) focuses on 'Where did it happen?' (Prepositions). Together, they provide a 3D understanding of the sentence.

section_6.title: Summary: From Attention to Intelligence
section_6.content: Summarize how these mathematical scores allow Transformers to process massive amounts of data in parallel, unlike older models that read word-by-word. This parallel 'scanning' is what makes ChatGPT and Claude possible.
section_6.example: Show a side-by-side comparison: An old robot reading a book line-by-line with a magnifying glass vs. a Transformer 'sensing' the entire page instantly through a web of interconnected attention lines.

outline.title: The Step-by-Step Calculation

outline.title: The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
outline.content: Define the three roles each word plays using a 'Library Search' analogy. 1. Query (Q): What I am looking for. 2. Key (K): The label on the shelf. 3. Value (V): The actual information inside the book.
outline.example: Imagine a Golden Retriever (the Query) looking for 'Food'. He checks various items (Keys): a 'Ball', a 'Leash', and a 'Bowl of Kibble'. The 'Bowl of Kibble' Key matches his Query best, so he focuses his attention on the contents (Value) of that bowl.

outline.title: Multi-Head Attention: Multiple Perspectives
outline.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough. LLMs use 'Multi-Head Attention' to look at different relationships simultaneously (e.g., grammar, rhyme, logic). Visualize this as several different colored spotlights shining on the same text.
outline.example: Head 1 (Red light) focuses on 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb). Head 2 (Blue light) focuses on 'Where did it happen?' (Prepositions). Together, they provide a 3D understanding of the sentence.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)"
        lines = [
            "Attention uses three distinct roles: Query, Key, and Value.",
            "Query represents the specific information we seek.",
            "Key acts as a label to match against Query.",
            "Similarity scores determine which Key matches the Query best.",
            "Value provides the actual information for the winning match."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        QUERY_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        KEY_COLOR = "#ADFF2F"
        VALUE_COLOR = "#00BFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Attention uses three distinct roles: Query, Key, and Value.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        q_label = Text("Query", color=QUERY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        k_label = Text("Key", color=KEY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        v_label = Text("Value", color=VALUE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(k_label, "A4")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k_label), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Query represents the specific information we seek.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        
        dog_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.4, color=QUERY_COLOR),
            Text("Dog", font_size=18, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        query_sub_label = Text("Seeking 'Food'", font_size=14, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dog_icon, "B2")
        query_sub_label.next_to(dog_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dog_icon), Write(query_sub_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Key acts as a label to match against Query.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(KEY_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Shelf items (Keys)
        key_ball = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Ball", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        key_leash = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Leash", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        key_kibble = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Kibble", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        
        self.place_at_grid(key_ball, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(key_leash, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(key_kibble, "D6")
        
        keys_group = VGroup(key_ball, key_leash, key_kibble)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(k) for k in keys_group], lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Similarity scores determine which Key matches the Query best.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Beam from Query to Kibble Key
        beam = Line(dog_icon.get_bottom(), key_kibble.get_top(), color=QUERY_COLOR, stroke_width=3)
        match_score = Text("Best Match!", font_size=18, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        match_score.next_to(key_kibble, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(beam))
        self.play(Write(match_score), key_kibble.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Value provides the actual information for the winning match.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(VALUE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Value Book
        book_box = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.8, color=VALUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        book_text = Text("Food", font_size=14, color=VALUE_COLOR)
        book_icon = VGroup(book_box, book_text)
        
        self.place_at_grid(book_icon, "E6")
        
        # Glow effect
        glow = Circle(radius=0.5, color=VALUE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=0).set_fill(VALUE_COLOR, opacity=0.3)
        glow.move_to(book_icon.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(book_icon))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(glow),
            book_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)"
        lines = [
            "Attention uses three distinct roles: Query, Key, and Value.",
            "Query represents the specific information we seek.",
            "Key acts as a label to match against Query.",
            "Similarity scores determine which Key matches the Query best.",
            "Value provides the actual information for the winning match."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        QUERY_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        KEY_COLOR = "#ADFF2F"
        VALUE_COLOR = "#00BFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Attention uses three distinct roles: Query, Key, and Value.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        q_label = Text("Query", color=QUERY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        k_label = Text("Key", color=KEY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        v_label = Text("Value", color=VALUE_COLOR, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(k_label, "A4")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(q_label), FadeIn(k_label), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Query represents the specific information we seek.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        
        dog_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.4, color=QUERY_COLOR),
            Text("Dog", font_size=18, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        query_sub_label = Text("Seeking 'Food'", font_size=14, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dog_icon, "B2")
        query_sub_label.next_to(dog_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dog_icon), Write(query_sub_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Key acts as a label to match against Query.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(KEY_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Shelf items (Keys)
        key_ball = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Ball", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        key_leash = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Leash", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        key_kibble = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.5, color=KEY_COLOR), Text("Kibble", font_size=16, color=KEY_COLOR))
        
        self.place_at_grid(key_ball, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(key_leash, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(key_kibble, "D6")
        
        keys_group = VGroup(key_ball, key_leash, key_kibble)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(k) for k in keys_group], lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Similarity scores determine which Key matches the Query best.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(QUERY_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Beam from Query to Kibble Key
        beam = Line(dog_icon.get_bottom(), key_kibble.get_top(), color=QUERY_COLOR, stroke_width=3)
        match_score = Text("Best Match!", font_size=18, color=QUERY_COLOR)
        match_score.next_to(key_kibble, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(beam))
        self.play(Write(match_score), key_kibble.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Value provides the actual information for the winning match.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(VALUE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Value Book
        book_box = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.8, color=VALUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        book_text = Text("Food", font_size=14, color=VALUE_COLOR)
        book_icon = VGroup(book_box, book_text)
        
        self.place_at_grid(book_icon, "E6")
        
        # Glow effect
        glow = Circle(radius=0.5, color=VALUE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=0).set_fill(VALUE_COLOR, opacity=0.3)
        glow.move_to(book_icon.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(book_icon))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(glow),
            book_icon.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors",
            [
                "Words can be represented as arrows called vectors.",
                "Directions indicate the meaning and relationship of words.",
                "Dot products measure how much these vectors align."
            ]
        )
        
        green_color = "#90EE90"  # Light green for 'Apple' and 'Fruit'
        pink_color = "#FFB6C1"   # Light pink for 'Apple' and 'Hammer'

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Vector Apple (Green)
        v_apple_g = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=green_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_apple_g = Text("Apple", font_size=20, color=green_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_apple_g, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(l_apple_g, "A2")
        
        # Create Vector Fruit (Green)
        v_fruit_g = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=green_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_fruit_g = Text("Fruit", font_size=20, color=green_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_fruit_g, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(l_fruit_g, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(v_apple_g), Write(l_apple_g))
        self.play(Create(v_fruit_g), Write(l_fruit_g))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Align Apple and Fruit (similar meaning)
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_angle(PI/6),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_angle(PI/6 + 0.15)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Introduce Apple and Hammer comparison (different meaning)
        # We reuse the concept but create new mobjects for the Pink set
        v_apple_p = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=pink_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_apple_p = Text("Apple", font_size=20, color=pink_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_apple_p, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(l_apple_p, "E2")

        v_hammer_p = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=pink_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_hammer_p = Text("Hammer", font_size=20, color=pink_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_hammer_p, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(l_hammer_p, "E4")

        # Fade out Green slightly and fade in Pink set
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            FadeIn(v_apple_p), FadeIn(l_apple_p),
            FadeIn(v_hammer_p), FadeIn(l_hammer_p)
        )
        
        # Orient Apple and Hammer in opposite directions
        self.play(
            v_apple_p.animate.set_angle(0),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_angle(PI - 0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define Similarity Counter
        sim_label = Text("Similarity Score:", font_size=24)
        sim_score = DecimalNumber(0.0, num_decimal_places=2, color=YELLOW)
        counter_group = VGroup(sim_label, sim_score).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_group, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(counter_group))
        
        # First: Show High similarity for Green vectors
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
        )
        self.play(ChangeDecimalToValue(sim_score, 0.95), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Second: Show Low similarity for Pink vectors
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.play(ChangeDecimalToValue(sim_score, -0.85), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

5.  **Performance Optimization**: Avoided `always_redraw` for expensive mobjects like `Text` and `DecimalNumber` to ensure smooth rendering within the time budget.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Summary: From Attention to Intelligence"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Attention enables models to process entire sequences at once.",
            "This parallel processing is much faster than reading word-by-word.",
            "It is the core engine driving modern AI intelligence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GRAY = "#808080"
        AQUA = "#7FFFD4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Lecture line index 0
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(AQUA))
        
        # Robot Icon (Simplified)
        robot_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
        robot_body = Square(side_length=0.3, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2).next_to(robot_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        robot = VGroup(robot_head, robot_body)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "B1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Sentence word-by-word
        words_list = ["The", "quick", "brown", "fox"]
        word_mobjects = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=18, color=GRAY) for w in words_list]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        # Position sentence at B2-B4 area
        self.place_in_area(word_mobjects, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Magnifying glass
        mg_lens = Circle(radius=0.12, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        mg_handle = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=[0.12, -0.12, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).next_to(mg_lens, DR, buff=-0.03)
        magnifying_glass = VGroup(mg_lens, mg_handle)
        magnifying_glass.move_to(word_mobjects[0].get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(word_mobjects), FadeIn(magnifying_glass))
        
        # Animate magnifying glass moving word-by-word
        for i in range(1, len(word_mobjects)):
            self.play(magnifying_glass.animate.move_to(word_mobjects[i].get_center()), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Lecture line index 1
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(AQUA)
        )
        
        # Transformer Grid Construction
        # Use area D2 to F5 for the grid
        grid_nodes = VGroup()
        node_positions = ["D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "E2", "E3", "E4", "E5", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"]
        
        for pos in node_positions:
            node = Circle(radius=0.08, color=AQUA, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=1)
            self.place_at_grid(node, pos)
            grid_nodes.add(node)
            
        # Connections (Web of interconnected lines)
        connections = VGroup()
        # To avoid performance issues and visual clutter, we connect a subset of nodes 
        # or use low opacity as instructed.
        for i in range(len(grid_nodes)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(grid_nodes)):
                line = Line(
                    grid_nodes[i].get_center(), 
                    grid_nodes[j].get_center(), 
                    color=AQUA, 
                    stroke_width=0.5, 
                    stroke_opacity=0.2
                )
                connections.add(line)
        
        # Simultaneous connection appearance
        self.play(
            Create(grid_nodes),
            Create(connections),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Lecture line index 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(AQUA)
        )
        
        # Pulse the entire grid with AQUA light
        # Using a flash/pulse effect
        pulse_overlay = grid_nodes.copy().set_fill(AQUA, opacity=1).set_stroke(AQUA, width=4)
        
        self.play(
            pulse_overlay.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0),
            connections.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.6, width=1),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.remove(pulse_overlay)

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

section_1.title: The Core Intuition: The 'It' Problem
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental problem of context in language. Explain how humans focus on specific words to understand meaning. Use a simple sentence to show how the word 'it' changes meaning based on the surrounding context.
section_1.example: Consider the sentences: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired' vs 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too wide'. In the first, 'it' is the animal; in the second, 'it' is the street. Attention is the mechanism that allows a computer to 'look' at the right words to figure this out.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors
section_2.content: Introduce vectors as arrows in space representing meaning. Explain the 'Dot Product' as a graphical tool: when two arrows point in the same direction, their product is high (they are similar). This is the mathematical 'glue' of attention.
section_2.example: Visualize two arrows: 'Apple' and 'Fruit' pointing almost in the same direction (high score), while 'Apple' and 'Hammer' point in opposite directions (low score).

section_3.title: The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
section_3.content: Define the three roles each word plays using a 'Library Search' analogy. 1. Query (Q): What I am looking for. 2. Key (K): The label on the shelf. 3. Value (V): The actual information inside the book.
section_3.example: Imagine a Golden Retriever (the Query) looking for 'Food'. He checks various items (Keys): a 'Ball', a 'Leash', and a 'Bowl of Kibble'. The 'Bowl of Kibble' Key matches his Query best, so he focuses his attention on the contents (Value) of that bowl.

section_4.title: The Step-by-Step Calculation
section_4.content: Break down the Attention formula: Score = (Q × K). Then, apply 'Softmax' to turn scores into percentages (weights) that add up to 100%. Finally, multiply these percentages by V to get the focused output. Use a heatmap visualization.
section_4.example: In the sentence 'The cat sat', when processing 'cat', the Q(cat) hits K(the) with 10% weight and K(sat) with 20% weight, but K(cat) itself with 70%. The resulting vector is a weighted mix of all three, heavily biased toward 'cat's' own identity and 'sat's' action.

section_5.title: Multi-Head Attention: Multiple Perspectives
section_5.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough. LLMs use 'Multi-Head Attention' to look at different relationships simultaneously (e.g., grammar, rhyme, logic). Visualize this as several different colored spotlights shining on the same text.
section_5.example: Head 1 (Red light) focuses on 'Who did what?' (Subject-Verb). Head 2 (Blue light) focuses on 'Where did it happen?' (Prepositions). Together, they provide a 3D understanding of the sentence.

section_6.title: Summary: From Attention to Intelligence
section_6.content: Summarize how these mathematical scores allow Transformers to process massive amounts of data in parallel, unlike older models that read word-by-word. This parallel 'scanning' is what makes ChatGPT and Claude possible.
section_6.example: Show a side-by-side comparison: An old robot reading a book line-by-line with a magnifying glass vs. a Transformer 'sensing' the entire page instantly through a web of interconnected attention lines.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Intuition: The 'It' Problem"
        lines = [

        self.play(FadeOut(s1), FadeOut(arrow1))
        
        s2_words_list = "The animal didn't cross the street because it was too wide.".split()

        self.play(Write(s2))
        
        # Indices: street(5), it(7)

        self.play(

            street_word_2.animate.set_color(COLOR_STREET)
        )
        
        arrow2 = CurvedArrow(it_word_2.get_bottom(), street_word_2.get_bottom(), color=COLOR_STREET, angle=TAU/4)
        self.play(Create(arrow2))
        
        # Flash labels
        label_animal = Text("REF: ANIMAL", font_size=18, color=COLOR_ANIMAL)

            Flash(label_street, color=COLOR_STREET)
        )

        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

            ]

        self.play(

            FadeIn(word_cat),
            FadeIn(word_sat),

        self.place_at_grid(score_70, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(score_20, "A4")
        
        self.play(Write(score_10), Write(score_70), Write(score_20))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transform scores into a colored heatmap where 'cat' glows in #FF4500.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        # Heatmap rectangles as visual anchors behind the words
        heat_the = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=0)

        self.place_at_grid(weight_20, "A4")

            ReplacementTransform(score_10, weight_10),
            ReplacementTransform(score_70, weight_70),
            ReplacementTransform(score_20, weight_20)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        val_color = "#90EE90"
        self.lecture[3].set_color(val_color)
        
        v1_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        v2_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        v3_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)

        v2_label = Text("V", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(v2_box)
        v3_label = Text("V", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(v3_box)
        
        v1 = VGroup(v1_box, v1_label)
        v2 = VGroup(v2_box, v2_label)
        v3 = VGroup(v3_box, v3_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "D4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), FadeIn(v3))
        
        # Scale based on weights 0.1, 0.7, 0.2

            v1.animate.scale(0.3),
            v2.animate.scale(1.1),
            v3.animate.scale(0.5)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        output_vec = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=1.2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        output_txt = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(output_vec)
        output_grp = VGroup(output_vec, output_txt)
        self.place_at_grid(output_grp, "F3")
        
        target_pos = self.grid["F3"]
        
        self.play(
            v1.animate.move_to(target_pos).set_opacity(0),
            v2.animate.move_to(target_pos).set_opacity(0),
            v3.animate.move_to(target_pos).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(output_grp, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        lecture_lines = [
            "Attention enables models to process entire sequences at once.",
            "This parallel processing is much faster than reading word-by-word.",
            "It is the core engine driving modern AI intelligence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GRAY = "#808080"
        AQUA = "#7FFFD4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Lecture line index 0
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(AQUA))
        
        # Robot Icon (Simplified)
        robot_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
        robot_body = Square(side_length=0.3, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2).next_to(robot_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        robot = VGroup(robot_head, robot_body)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "B1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Sentence word-by-word
        words_list = ["The", "quick", "brown", "fox"]
        word_mobjects = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=18, color=GRAY) for w in words_list]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        # Position sentence at B2-B4 area
        self.place_in_area(word_mobjects, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Magnifying glass
        mg_lens = Circle(radius=0.12, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        mg_handle = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=[0.12, -0.12, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).next_to(mg_lens, DR, buff=-0.03)
        magnifying_glass = VGroup(mg_lens, mg_handle)
        magnifying_glass.move_to(word_mobjects[0].get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(word_mobjects), FadeIn(magnifying_glass))
        
        # Animate magnifying glass moving word-by-word

            self.play(magnifying_glass.animate.move_to(word_mobjects[i].get_center()), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Lecture line index 1
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(AQUA)
        )
        
        # Transformer Grid Construction
        # Use area D2 to F5 for the grid
        grid_nodes = VGroup()
        node_positions = ["D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "E2", "E3", "E4", "E5", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"]
        
        for pos in node_positions:
            node = Circle(radius=0.08, color=AQUA, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=1)
            self.place_at_grid(node, pos)
            grid_nodes.add(node)
            
        # Connections (Web of interconnected lines)
        connections = VGroup()
        # To avoid performance issues and visual clutter, we connect a subset of nodes 
        # or use low opacity as instructed.
        for i in range(len(grid_nodes)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(grid_nodes)):
                line = Line(
                    grid_nodes[i].get_center(), 
                    grid_nodes[j].get_center(), 
                    color=AQUA, 
                    stroke_width=0.5, 
                    stroke_opacity=0.2
                )
                connections.add(line)
        
        # Simultaneous connection appearance
        self.play(
            Create(grid_nodes),
            Create(connections),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Lecture line index 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(AQUA)
        )
        
        # Pulse the entire grid with AQUA light

        pulse_overlay = grid_nodes.copy().set_fill(AQUA, opacity=1).set_stroke(AQUA, width=4)
        
        self.play(
            pulse_overlay.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0),
            connections.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.6, width=1),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.remove(pulse_overlay)
        # Final subtle glow
        self.play(
            grid_nodes.animate.set_color(AQUA),
            connections.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3, width=0.5),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

The video production is progressing well, with initial Manim code generated and rendered for all six sections. Automatic video reviews have identified several layout and spacing issues across all sections, and these are now being addressed.

### **Current Project Status**
*   **Initial Rendering Complete:** All sections (1–6) have had their first renders reviewed.
*   **Refinement Phase:** Every section is currently undergoing layout adjustments to resolve overlapping elements, vertical crowding, and margin issues.
*   **Asset Integration:** Sections 2, 3, 4, and 6 are also integrating specific visual assets (icons for Apple, Dog, Cat, etc.) as requested by the storyboard.

### **Key Coordination Actions**
1.  **Code Generation Tasks Finalized:** The original tasks for building the Manim code (Issues #3, #6, #9, #12, #15, #18) have been marked as complete following the successful initial renders.
2.  **Layout & Logic Fixes Routed:**
    *   **Section 1:** Coder1 is adjusting label positioning and vertical spacing to avoid overlaps with attention indicators.
    *   **Section 2:** Coder2 is resolving vector overlaps in the center and aligning labels for consistency. I have also requested the "Similarity Score" be moved slightly to avoid the bottom edge.
    *   **Section 3:** Coder3 is re-aligning Key/Query/Value objects to ensure the mapping relationships are visually clear and categorization is logical.
    *   **Section 4:** Coder4 is shifting elements to the right to create better margins with the lecture text and cleaning up the heatmap/output positioning.
    *   **Section 5:** Coder5 is moving the main sentence and Head labels to prevent obstruction of the lecture notes.
    *   **Section 6:** Coder6 is repositioning the robot icon and expanding the neural network visualization to make the "parallel processing" concept more impactful.
3.  **Asset Integration:** Specific issues (#20, #21, #22, #23) remain active for coders to swap out generic shapes for the high-quality assets defined in the storyboard.

The team is now focused on these targeted improvements to ensure a professional and clear final presentation for university students.

outline.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors
outline.content: Introduce vectors as arrows in space representing meaning. Explain the 'Dot Product' as a graphical tool: when two arrows point in the same direction, their product is high (they are similar). This is the mathematical 'glue' of attention.
outline.example: Visualize two arrows: 'Apple' and 'Fruit' pointing almost in the same direction (high score), while 'Apple' and 'Hammer' point in opposite directions (low score).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors
lecture_lines: Words can be represented as arrows called vectors.
Directions indicate the meaning and relationship of words.
Dot products measure how much these vectors align.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: Measuring Similarity with Vectors",
            [
                "Words can be represented as arrows called vectors.",
                "Directions indicate the meaning and relationship of words.",
                "Dot products measure how much these vectors align."
            ]
        )
        
        green_color = "#90EE90"  # Light green for 'Apple' and 'Fruit'
        pink_color = "#FFB6C1"   # Light pink for 'Apple' and 'Hammer'

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Vector Apple (Green)
        v_apple_g = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=green_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_apple_g = Text("Apple", font_size=20, color=green_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_apple_g, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(l_apple_g, "A2")
        
        # Create Vector Fruit (Green)
        v_fruit_g = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=green_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_fruit_g = Text("Fruit", font_size=20, color=green_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_fruit_g, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(l_fruit_g, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(v_apple_g), Write(l_apple_g))
        self.play(Create(v_fruit_g), Write(l_fruit_g))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Align Apple and Fruit (similar meaning)
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_angle(PI/6),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_angle(PI/6 + 0.15)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Introduce Apple and Hammer comparison (different meaning)
        # We reuse the concept but create new mobjects for the Pink set
        v_apple_p = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=pink_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_apple_p = Text("Apple", font_size=20, color=pink_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_apple_p, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(l_apple_p, "E2")

        v_hammer_p = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=pink_color, stroke_width=4, buff=0)
        l_hammer_p = Text("Hammer", font_size=20, color=pink_color)
        self.place_at_grid(v_hammer_p, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(l_hammer_p, "E4")

        # Fade out Green slightly and fade in Pink set
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            FadeIn(v_apple_p), FadeIn(l_apple_p),
            FadeIn(v_hammer_p), FadeIn(l_hammer_p)
        )
        
        # Orient Apple and Hammer in opposite directions
        self.play(
            v_apple_p.animate.set_angle(0),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_angle(PI - 0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define Similarity Counter
        sim_label = Text("Similarity Score:", font_size=24)
        sim_score = DecimalNumber(0.0, num_decimal_places=2, color=YELLOW)
        counter_group = VGroup(sim_label, sim_score).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_group, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(counter_group))
        
        # First: Show High similarity for Green vectors
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
        )
        self.play(ChangeDecimalToValue(sim_score, 0.95), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Second: Show Low similarity for Pink vectors
        self.play(
            v_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_apple_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            l_fruit_g.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            v_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_apple_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            v_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
            l_hammer_p.animate.set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.play(ChangeDecimalToValue(sim_score, -0.85), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Step-by-Step Calculation
outline.content: Break down the Attention formula: Score = (Q × K). Then, apply 'Softmax' to turn scores into percentages (weights) that add up to 100%. Finally, multiply these percentages by V to get the focused output. Use a heatmap visualization.
outline.example: In the sentence 'The cat sat', when processing 'cat', the Q(cat) hits K(the) with 10% weight and K(sat) with 20% weight, but K(cat) itself with 70%. The resulting vector is a weighted mix of all three, heavily biased toward 'cat's' own identity and 'sat's' action.

storyboard.title: The Step-by-Step Calculation
lecture_lines: First, calculate similarity by multiplying Query and Key vectors.
These raw scores indicate how words relate to each other.
Softmax converts these scores into normalized probability weights.
Multiply weights by Value vectors to aggregate the information.
The final output highlights the most relevant context.
animations: Show text 'The cat sat' with a 'Query' pointer over 'cat' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] in #FFFFFF.
Display numerical scores (10, 70, 20) over 'The', 'cat' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png], and 'sat' in #FFFF00.
Transform scores into a colored heatmap where 'cat' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png] glows in #FF4500.
Show three 'Value' boxes scaling their size based on the heatmap intensities.
Merge the scaled boxes into a single 'Output' vector in #00FFFF.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Step-by-Step Calculation",
            [
                "First, calculate similarity by multiplying Query and Key vectors.",
                "These raw scores indicate how words relate to each other.",
                "Softmax converts these scores into normalized probability weights.",
                "Multiply weights by Value vectors to aggregate the information.",
                "The final output highlights the most relevant context."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show text 'The cat sat' with a 'Query' pointer over 'cat' in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        word_the = Text("The", font_size=24)
        word_cat = Text("cat", font_size=24)
        word_sat = Text("sat", font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(word_the, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(word_cat, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(word_sat, "B4")
        
        query_arrow = Arrow(DOWN, UP, color=WHITE, buff=0.1).scale(0.5)
        query_label = Text("Query", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        query_ptr = VGroup(query_arrow, query_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(query_ptr, "C3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(word_the),
            FadeIn(word_cat),
            FadeIn(word_sat),
            FadeIn(query_ptr)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display numerical scores (10, 70, 20) over 'The', 'cat', and 'sat' in #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        score_10 = Text("10", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        score_70 = Text("70", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        score_20 = Text("20", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(score_10, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(score_70, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(score_20, "A4")
        
        self.play(Write(score_10), Write(score_70), Write(score_20))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transform scores into a colored heatmap where 'cat' glows in #FF4500.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        # Heatmap rectangles as visual anchors behind the words
        heat_the = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=0)
        heat_cat = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0)
        heat_sat = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(heat_the, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(heat_cat, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(heat_sat, "B4")
        
        # Softmax weights replacing raw scores
        weight_10 = Text("0.1", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        weight_70 = Text("0.7", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        weight_20 = Text("0.2", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        
        self.place_at_grid(weight_10, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_70, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_20, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(heat_the), FadeIn(heat_cat), FadeIn(heat_sat),
            ReplacementTransform(score_10, weight_10),
            ReplacementTransform(score_70, weight_70),
            ReplacementTransform(score_20, weight_20)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show three 'Value' boxes scaling their size based on the heatmap intensities.
        val_color = "#90EE90"
        self.lecture[3].set_color(val_color)
        
        v1_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        v2_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        v3_box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=val_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        v1_label = Text("V", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(v1_box)

outline.title: The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
outline.content: Define the three roles each word plays using a 'Library Search' analogy. 1. Query (Q): What I am looking for. 2. Key (K): The label on the shelf. 3. Value (V): The actual information inside the book.
outline.example: Imagine a Golden Retriever (the Query) looking for 'Food'. He checks various items (Keys): a 'Ball', a 'Leash', and a 'Bowl of Kibble'. The 'Bowl of Kibble' Key matches his Query best, so he focuses his attention on the contents (Value) of that bowl.

storyboard.title: The Trinity: Query, Key, and Value (Q, K, V)
lecture_lines: Attention uses three distinct roles: Query, Key, and Value.
Query represents the specific information we seek.
Key acts as a label to match against Query.
Similarity scores determine which Key matches the Query best.
Value provides the actual information for the winning match.

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Step-by-Step Calculation",
            [
                "First, calculate similarity by multiplying Query and Key vectors.",
                "These raw scores indicate how words relate to each other.",
                "Softmax converts these scores into normalized probability weights.",
                "Multiply weights by Value vectors to aggregate the information.",
                "The final output highlights the most relevant context."
            ]
        )

        # Asset path
        cat_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show text 'The cat sat' with a 'Query' pointer over 'cat' [Asset: cat.png] in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        word_the = Text("The", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        word_sat = Text("sat", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # Integrate Asset for 'cat'
        cat_icon = ImageMobject(cat_asset).scale(0.4)
        word_cat_label = Text("cat", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        cat_obj = VGroup(cat_icon, word_cat_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(word_the, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(cat_obj, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(word_sat, "B5")
        
        query_arrow = Arrow(DOWN, UP, color=WHITE, buff=0.1).scale(0.5)
        query_label = Text("Query", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        query_ptr = VGroup(query_arrow, query_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(query_ptr, "C4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(word_the),
            FadeIn(cat_obj),
            FadeIn(word_sat),
            FadeIn(query_ptr)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display numerical scores (10, 70, 20) over 'The', 'cat' [Asset: cat.png], and 'sat' in #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        score_10 = Text("10", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        score_70 = Text("70", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        score_20 = Text("20", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(score_10, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(score_70, "A4")
        self.place_at_grid(score_20, "A5")
        
        self.play(Write(score_10), Write(score_70), Write(score_20))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transform scores into a colored heatmap where 'cat' [Asset: cat.png] glows in #FF4500.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        # Heatmap rectangles as visual anchors behind the words
        heat_the = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=0)
        heat_cat = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=1.0, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.7, stroke_width=0)
        heat_sat = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, fill_color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(heat_the, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(heat_cat, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(heat_sat, "B5")
        
        # Softmax weights replacing raw scores
        weight_10 = Text("0.1", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        weight_70 = Text("0.7", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        weight_20 = Text("0.2", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        
        self.place_at_grid(weight_10, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_70, "A4")
        self.place_at_grid(weight_20, "A5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(heat_the), FadeIn(heat_cat), FadeIn(heat_sat),
            ReplacementTransform(score_10, weight_10),
            ReplacementTransform(score_70, weight_70),
            ReplacementTransform(score_20, weight_20)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Multiply weights by Value vectors to aggregate the information.
        val_color = "#90EE90"
        self.lecture[3].set_color(val_color)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
